title: Annotatio III §.VII: Innocent’s allocution — Dunelm: rival of Christ, not mere Vicar, when the article is thrust
pass_a_gloss: The author of so great a Canonization betrays himself by his sermons, as a shrew by its voice, addressing his own in this manner: To me, he says, it is said in the Prophet: I have set you over nations and kingdoms &c. When the most praiseworthy Dunelm had reviewed all these allocutions of Innocent at p. 149, he adds at p. 150: These things that one, already made not only Vicar but even Rival of Christ, I now commemorate, that we may see what the condition of affairs and the face of the Latin Church was when Transsubstantiation was proposed and thrust by Pope Innocent as an article of faith.
pass_b_english: Innocent betrays the author of the canonization in his own sermons — ‘To me it is said in the Prophet: I have set you over nations and kingdoms…’ (as a shrew by its voice).
Dunelm (pp. 149–150): commemorate this already Rival of Christ, not mere Vicar, to see the Latin Church’s face when Transsubstantiation was thrust as an article of faith.
source_text: Auctor tantæ Canonizationis se sermonibus suis, ceu sorex voce, prodit, hunc in modum suos allocutus: Mihi, inquit, dicitur in Propheta: Constitui te super gentes & regna &c. &c. Has Innocentii allocutiones omnes cum laudatissimus Dunelmensis pag. 149. recensuisset, subjicit pag. 150: Hæc ille Christi jam factus, non Vicarius modo, sed etiam Rivalis, quæ nunc commemoro, ut videamus qualis fuerit rerum conditio & Latinæ Ecclesiæ facies, quando Transsubstantiatio pro fidei articulo ab Innocentio Papa proposita est & obtrusa.
